produzione.metaDescription: Every product is made in multiple stages to nautical industry standards: European-made AISI 316 steel, TIG welding, polishing, painting. Viareggio, since 1999.
produzione.heroSub: It starts with a steel bar six metres long. It ends as a shower column. In between there are more stages than you would expect, and several of them are still done by hand.
produzione.heroImageAlt: Stainless steel bars being worked at the Fontealta plant in Viareggio.
produzione.f1P1: The steel arrives in six-metre bars, laser marked at source with diameter, wall thickness, heat number, batch and exact production date. Every tube is inspected on arrival.
produzione.f1P2: It means that for every column leaving here we know which heat it came from. This is not paperwork: it is what makes it possible, years later, to trace a piece back to its origin.
produzione.f1Alt: Six-metre AISI 316 stainless steel bars, laser marked at source.
produzione.f2P1: The bars are cut exactly in half: three metres, the developed length of the tallest models. No offcuts, nothing left unusable.
produzione.f2P2: On the Twiggy series the cut is set at thirty degrees, made while the tube is still straight. At that point in the process it looks like a mistake. It compensates for the way the metal shifts during bending, so that the head of the column ends up perfectly parallel to the ground.
produzione.f2Alt: A stainless steel bar being cut at its mid point.
produzione.f3P1: Cold bending a tube with a wall thicker than three millimetres without crushing it takes a part no customer will ever see: a moving mandrel in bronze and aluminium alloy that goes inside the tube and holds the section round while the bending machine works.
produzione.f3P2: The mandrel alone is not enough. The elasticity of steel changes imperceptibly from one heat to the next, and two tubes with the same specification react slightly differently. At the start of every batch the bend angle is recalibrated by hand: bend, measure, correct.
produzione.f3Alt: A bending machine working a thick-walled stainless steel tube.
produzione.f4P1: In our workshop, CNC machining centres mill the internal bodies of the timed taps and the mechanical components from solid. The technical sheet of each piece states what it is made of.
produzione.f4P2: Milling from solid instead of assembling means fewer joints, and every joint saved is one less place where something can give way.
produzione.f4Alt: Stainless steel components milled from solid on a CNC machining centre.
produzione.f5P1: The external structures are consolidated with TIG welding. It is the slowest method available and it is the one that holds on the largest structures.
produzione.f5Alt: TIG welding on an external stainless steel structure.
produzione.f6P1: This is the stage the customer never sees and the one that decides everything else.
produzione.f6P2: Raw steel has a natural porosity: microscopic openings where corrosion can take hold. The surface is polished with abrasive papers of increasing grit, then with flap brush machines and cotton wheels, which close the pores for good.
produzione.f6P3: Only then can the chromium oxide layer, the one that makes steel stainless, wrap the whole surface without leaving weak points. A mirror finish is not a flourish: it is the sign that nothing underneath has been left open.
produzione.f6Alt: Polishing a stainless steel surface with flap brushes.
produzione.f7P1: This is where the column takes on its skin: mirror, brushed, painted and PVD. There are seven finishes in the catalogue. Colour is another matter: it has no number, because painting has no limits. RAL, Pantone or NCS, even on a single piece.
produzione.f7Alt: Stainless steel shower columns in different finishes side by side.
produzione.f8P1: Painted parts dry naturally, at room temperature, for two weeks. That is two of the five we quote as production time.
produzione.f8P2: An oven would do the same job in under an hour, but it would harden the paint and make it rigid. An outdoor column goes from minus twenty degrees in winter to over sixty on a surface in full sun, and with every cycle the steel expands. A rigid paint cracks sooner or later. A slowly dried paint stays elastic and follows the metal.
produzione.f8P3: Two weeks of waiting against ten years of durability.
produzione.f8Alt: Painted parts drying naturally at room temperature.
produzione.f9P1: Inside, the plumbing is fitted, with every connection working to millimetric tolerances. The handles receive the Fontealta laser marking, which authenticates the piece. Every column is hydraulically tested before it leaves.
produzione.f9P2: The last step is a soft non-woven bag, then shock-proof packing: because the riskiest part of the journey, for a mirror polished and painted piece, is often the last one.
produzione.f9Alt: Fitting the internal plumbing and testing a shower column.
produzione.chiusuraP: We do not work to be fast. We work so the piece holds up outside, in salt and sun, for years to come.
produzione.chiusuraDidascalia: Illustrated reconstruction of the Viareggio workshop.
produzione.formH2: Want to see how we work?

chiSiamo.metaDescription: Since 1999 in Viareggio we have worked AISI 316 stainless steel: freestanding shower columns, taps, made-to-measure colour. Two trades, one idea.
chiSiamo.heroSub: Since 1999 we have worked AISI 316 stainless steel in Viareggio, by the sea, where salt puts every surface to the test.
chiSiamo.s1P1: Fontealta was born in Viareggio in February 1999, from the meeting of two skills that rarely speak to each other.
chiSiamo.s1P2: On one side, taps and fittings. Andrea Farnocchia’s father had spent a lifetime there: he knew how to make water flow inside a metal body, which tolerances matter and which things break.
chiSiamo.s1P3: On the other, boatbuilding. Andrea came from studies in that field, where the first question about a material is never whether it is beautiful, but how well it resists salt.
chiSiamo.s1P4: From that meeting came a choice that seemed eccentric at the time: making high-end taps in stainless steel, instead of chrome-plated brass like everyone else.
chiSiamo.s1ImageAlt: Fontealta craftsman working on a steel mixer
chiSiamo.s2P1: By the sea, steel meets salt every day: that is why it takes marine steel.
chiSiamo.s2P2: Between AISI 304 and AISI 316 there are a few percentage points of molybdenum. That little is what slows pitting corrosion, the kind that starts from an invisible point and spreads from there.
chiSiamo.s2P3: 316 costs more and is harder to work: it slows down every stage of production, and its extra nickel and molybdenum make it a more expensive raw material.
chiSiamo.s2P4: Our shower columns and steel taps are AISI 316. And the steel we work is exclusively of European production.
chiSiamo.s3P1: Freestanding shower columns, bathroom taps, solutions for kitchens and for yachts. Twenty collections, over five hundred articles, seven catalogue finishes and any colour on request: RAL, Pantone or NCS, even on a single piece, with no minimum order.
chiSiamo.s3P2: We design and manufacture in-house, from raw tube to hydraulic testing. The production cycle is entirely Italian: machine precision where the machine is needed, the craftsman’s hand where the machine cannot reach.
chiSiamo.s3P3: When a project asks for something that does not exist, we build it. It is a habit we have from working on megayachts, where the standard piece is almost never enough.
chiSiamo.s4P1: Viareggio is not an address. It is the reason we can do certain things.
chiSiamo.s4P2: The shipyards gave us suppliers who work steel to yacht-building standards: a flaw that would go unnoticed elsewhere is immediately flagged here, and becomes a reject.
chiSiamo.s4P3: The beach clubs and hotels of the coast are our proving ground: a shower that survives a summer on the beach has already surpassed any domestic use.
chiSiamo.s4P4: And then there is the Carnival. The floats are structures up to twenty metres tall, rebuilt from scratch every year and hand-painted in whatever shade is needed. Around them, and around the megayacht painters, Viareggio has grown a network of specialists with no equivalent in the rest of Italy.
chiSiamo.s4P5: They are the same suppliers we turn to. That is why an off-catalogue shade on a single piece is, for us, a normal request and not an exception to negotiate.
chiSiamo.s5P1: Our shower columns and steel taps are always AISI 316, and can be installed anywhere. The differences lie elsewhere, and there are three.
chiSiamo.s5P2: The finish, because not all of them respond the same way to the exposure and maintenance the project will be able to guarantee. The equipment, because it changes according to the system in place or the one that can be brought in. The installation, because it depends on who will use the product and how often.
chiSiamo.s5P3: These are the questions we ask before proposing anything. It is not commercial courtesy: it is how we avoid a designer finding themselves, three years after delivery, answering for a choice that could have been made better.
chiSiamo.s5P4: Our work ends when the project holds over time. Not when the order is placed.
chiSiamo.formH2: The rest we tell in person.
chiSiamo.formIntro: Tell us about your project: from private residences to hospitality, all the way to megayachts.

This notice describes how the personal data of users who consult the Site and use its contact, catalogue request and newsletter subscription forms is processed, pursuant to art. 13 of EU Regulation 2016/679 (“GDPR”) and Italian Legislative Decree 196/2003 as amended by Italian Legislative Decree 101/2018.

Rubinetteria F & F L’Artigiana S.r.l., Via Libeccio 13/15, 55049 Viareggio (LU), Italy, VAT number IT01718720467, email info@fontealta.it, certified email (PEC) fontealta_lartigiana@pec.it. The data controller may be contacted for any request concerning personal data at the details indicated above. The Company has not appointed a Data Protection Officer, as the legal requirements for doing so are not met.

Contact form. First name, surname, email, telephone number (optional), company (optional) and type of enquiry, chosen from quote, consultation and other. In addition: country, notes (optional; required for the “other” enquiry type or with “Other country”) and the language in which the Site is browsed, detected automatically. Purpose: to respond to requests for information and quotations. Legal basis: performance of pre-contractual measures at the request of the data subject (art. 6.1.b GDPR) and the data controller’s legitimate interest in responding (art. 6.1.f). After sending, the data subject receives at the address provided an automatic email confirming receipt, sent through Brevo. Sending the request does not entail subscribing to the newsletter, which happens only if the data subject ticks the dedicated optional box.

Catalogue request. Name, surname, email and country; notes only with “Other country”, to specify it. In addition: the language in which the Site is browsed, detected automatically. Purpose: to send by email the requested catalogue in PDF, in the language of the country indicated, and to respond to the request. Sending the request does not entail subscribing to the newsletter, which happens only if the data subject ticks the dedicated optional box. Legal basis: performance of pre-contractual measures at the request of the data subject (art. 6.1.b GDPR) and the data controller’s legitimate interest in responding (art. 6.1.f).

Newsletter and commercial communications. Data: email, name, surname, country (not requested by the form in the footer), language of the Site, page of origin, date, time and version of the consent text. Purpose: sending by email the newsletter and commercial communications about Fontealta’s products, collections, projects and events, and measuring, in aggregate and individually, the opening of messages and clicks, in order to improve their content. Legal basis: the data subject’s consent (art. 6.1.a GDPR and art. 130 of Italian Legislative Decree 196/2003), given by ticking the optional box when a contact or catalogue request form is sent, or by subscribing with the newsletter form in the footer of the Site, which asks for the name, surname and email and the ticking of the box. Consent is optional: refusing it does not prevent or condition the response to requests or the sending of the catalogue. Consent can be withdrawn at any time using the unsubscribe link in every email or by writing to info@fontealta.it, without affecting the lawfulness of the processing based on consent before its withdrawal (art. 7.3 GDPR).

Technical browsing data. IP address, browser and device type, pages requested, timestamps, processed by hosting and distribution providers for the operation and security of the Site (protection against attacks, diagnostics). Legal basis: legitimate interest (art. 6.1.f). This data is not used to identify the user.

Usage statistics. The Site uses Vercel Web Analytics, which does not employ cookies or persistent identifiers and collects aggregated data (pages visited, referrer, country, device type). This does not constitute profiling and no consent is required.

The Site does not provide for public account registration, does not carry out profiling and does not make automated decisions. Commercial communications are sent only to those who have given their consent in the manner described above. The provision of data marked as mandatory in the form is necessary to follow up on the request; without it, the request cannot be processed. Consent to the newsletter, on the other hand, is optional.
The data may be processed, on behalf of the data controller, by suppliers appointed as data processors pursuant to art. 28 GDPR:

blocchi.li: Vercel Inc.: hosting, web infrastructure and usage statistics
Zapier Inc.: forwarding to the data controller of enquiries sent through the forms on the Site

Sendinblue SAS (Brevo), 17 rue Salneuve, 75017 Paris, France: sending of the email with the requested catalogue and of the automatic email confirming contact requests, sending of the newsletter and management of subscriptions and unsubscriptions
Cloudflare Inc.: hosting and distribution of videos

blocchi.p: The Contact page embeds a Google Maps map, provided by Google Ireland Ltd.: when the map loads, Google receives technical browsing data, including the IP address, and processes it in accordance with its own privacy notice.

The data may also be accessed by Company personnel authorised to process it and, where necessary, by consultants, resellers or area agents in order to follow up on the request, within the limits of the purpose. The data is not disseminated or transferred to third parties for their own purposes.

blocchi.h3: Transfer of data outside the European Union

blocchi.p: Some suppliers, including Google for the map on the Contact page, are based in the United States or transfer data there. Transfers take place on the basis of appropriate safeguards pursuant to artt. 44-49 GDPR: Standard Contractual Clauses adopted by the European Commission and, where applicable, the supplier’s adherence to the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. A copy of the safeguards may be requested from the data controller.

The data collected through the contact form is retained for the time necessary to handle the request and, in any case, for a maximum of 24 months from the last contact, save for different legal obligations or the establishment of a contractual relationship, in which case the retention periods provided for commercial and tax documentation apply. Technical browsing data is retained by the suppliers for the time strictly necessary for security purposes, generally not exceeding 30 days.

The data processed for the newsletter is retained until consent is withdrawn and, in any case, for no more than 24 months from the last interaction with the communications received, after which it is erased. After withdrawal or erasure, the data controller retains only the email address and the information on the consent and its withdrawal, for the time necessary to demonstrate the lawfulness of the processing and to respect the data subject’s wish not to receive further communications (art. 6.1.c and 6.1.f GDPR).
The logs of the emails sent are retained by Brevo for 24 months.

The data subject may exercise at any time the rights provided for by artt. 15-22 GDPR: access to their data, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, portability, objection to processing based on legitimate interest and, at any time and without giving reasons, to processing for marketing purposes (art. 21.2 GDPR), and withdrawal of consent (art. 7.3 GDPR). Requests should be sent to info@fontealta.it. The data controller responds within one month, extendable in the cases provided for by law.

The data subject has the right to lodge a complaint with the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (the Italian Data Protection Authority) (www.gpdp.it) if they believe that the processing of their data infringes the GDPR, without prejudice to any other administrative or judicial remedy.

The data controller adopts technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk: encrypted connections (HTTPS), access control to the CMS, qualified suppliers bound by agreements pursuant to art. 28 GDPR, protections against automated submissions on the contact form.
This notice may be updated; the version in force is the one published on this page with the date of last update.

This cookie policy explains which cookies and similar technologies the Site uses, pursuant to art. 122 of Italian Legislative Decree 196/2003 and the Guidelines of the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (the Italian Data Protection Authority) of 10 June 2021.

Cookies are small text files that websites save on the user’s device in order to function correctly or to collect information. They are divided into technical cookies, necessary for the operation and provision of the service requested by the user, for which no consent is required, and profiling or third-party cookies for marketing purposes, which require prior consent.

The Site exclusively uses technical and functional cookies. It does not use profiling, marketing or third-party cookies for such purposes, and does not transfer data to third parties for such purposes. Accordingly, pursuant to the Guidelines of the Garante, no prior consent is required and no consent banner is present.

blocchi.li: NEXT_LOCALE: stores the language of the pages visited, to show content in the correct language. Duration: session. Purpose: functional. First party.

Content preview cookies (__prerender_bypass, sanity-preview-perspective, sanity-preview-variant, sanity-preview-partitioned): set only for Site administrators while editing content in the CMS. Duration: session. Purpose: technical. First party.

blocchi.p: For usage statistics, the Site uses Vercel Web Analytics, which does not employ cookies or persistent identifiers and collects aggregated data (pages visited, referrer, country, device type). This does not constitute profiling and no consent is required.

The Contact page embeds a Google Maps map. In the configuration adopted by the Site, the map does not set cookies (checked on 16 September 2026); it does, however, receive technical browsing data, as described in the privacy notice. Should Google change this behaviour, a consent banner will be activated before the map loads.

The videos on the Site are distributed by Cloudflare Inc. without cookies. The Site does not embed any other third-party widgets or scripts, from social networks or advertising platforms. Any links to third-party websites (social media, trade fairs, partners) lead to websites that apply their own cookie policies.

The user may block or delete cookies through their browser settings. Disabling technical cookies may compromise certain functionalities of the Site, such as the memory of the language. Instructions are available in the guides for Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge.

This cookie policy may be updated over time; changes will be published on this page. Should analytics tools using cookies or profiling tools be introduced in the future, a compliant consent banner will be activated before they load.
